key_insight: Experimentally trained surrogate models can forecast cylinder-wake evolution faster than real time, but their accuracy degrades when transient features, noise, and missing observations dominate.
engineering_relevance: These models are promising for flow control and other engineering tasks where quick predictions are needed from imperfect experimental measurements.
method: Train FCNNs, U-Nets, Fourier neural operators, and DMD-based models on 2D, 2-component PIV wake data.
Test extended-horizon forecasting at fixed Re = 590.
Evaluate robustness across Re = 230 to 2920 to probe effects of increasing turbulence and 3D behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports meaningful short-term forecasts and faster-than-real-time evaluation, but lower fidelity for high-frequency content and transient structures under noisy or incomplete inputs.
watch_item: Do not assume good long-horizon accuracy from sparse or noisy measurements, especially for higher-Re flows where unobserved 3D effects grow.
paper_title: Data-driven surrogate models for forecasting experimentally measured fluid flows
